headline: US electronics factory-gate prices rise fastest on record
text:
# US electronics factory-gate prices rise fastest on record

Chip-adjacent US prices are up 12.9% on the year while Europe's odd moves — Austrian power bills, Austrian pharma, Hungarian mining — all look like level shifts, not trends.

## Today in the data

### US electronics prices up 12.9%
[US electronics factory-gate prices and chip output, yoy](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
US PPI for computer and electronic products stood at 120.0 in Aug 2026, up 12.9% on the year (us-ppi-sectors), against a usual +0.6%. The chart shows the rise settling into a plateau above 10% since Mar 2026, alongside semiconductor output up 11.9% in Jul 2026 (us-chips). Caveat: the PPI is not seasonally adjusted and base periods differ by series, so only ratios and growth rates are comparable.

### Austrian power bills jump a third
[Household electricity price, EUR/kWh, all taxes (2008-2025)](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
Austrian households paid €0.3272/kWh in H2 2025, up 34.3% on H2 2024 and the biggest rise since 2008 (energy-household-eu). Luxembourg rose 31.7% to €0.2665 in the same half; Germany, at €0.3869, remains dearer. Caveat: the 2024-S2 base is itself a dip (€0.2437 after €0.2731 in 2024-S1), so part of the jump is a base effect worth checking against the withdrawal of tax and levy relief.

### Austrian pharma output halves
[Austrian pharma production against total manufacturing, 2021=100](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
Austrian pharma production (C21) was 160.4 in Jul 2026, down 45.7% on a year earlier and the sharpest fall since the series starts in 2011 (eu-ipi-sectors). Total manufacturing sat at 102.6 the same month, so this is one sector, not the economy. Caveat: the pharma line is extremely spiky — a single plant's batch timing moves it — and the July point is a first estimate open to revision.

### Hungarian mining doubles
[Hungarian mining output doubles, 2021=100](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
Hungarian mining and quarrying is reported at 155.7 in Jul 2026, up 101.9% on the year, the biggest rise since Sep 2018 (eu-mining-ipi, today's note). The chart steps up from 85.0 in Mar 2026 to 138.3 in Jun — a level shift, not a drift. Caveat: get_series returns the Hungarian line only through Jun 2026, so the July point is not yet drawn; Poland's index (121.2) shows no such break.

### UK coal power all but gone
[UK electricity generation by source, TWh, 1985-2025](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
UK coal generation was 0.33 TWh in 2025, down 82.6% on 2024 and the sharpest fall in a record from 1921 (electricity-mix). On the chart, wind at 85.8 TWh has drawn level with gas at 90.9 TWh, while nuclear is 36.4 TWh. Caveat: the last year is often Ember's provisional figure, and this is generation, not consumption — imports are not shown.

### Estonia's new-car market halves
[New car registrations in Estonia by fuel, 2014-2025](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
Estonia registered 13,141 new cars in 2025, down 49% on 2024, with diesel down 70.4% to 1,738 (eu-car-registrations). Electric registrations were 872, so the diesel collapse is not being offset within the chart. Caveat: the record starts only in 2014 and a car-tax change from 2025 is worth checking against as the cause of the timing.

### Egypt's FDI drops 31bn dollars
[Egypt net FDI inflows, current USD, 1990-2025](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
Egypt's net FDI inflows were $15.45bn in 2025, $31.1bn below 2024, the sharpest fall since 1971 (macro-external). The chart shows 2024 as a lone spike well outside the $8–12bn band of the 2010s, so 2025 is closer to normal than the fall suggests. Caveat: annual World Bank data lagging one to two years; the 2024 spike is worth checking against one-off land-sale inflows.

## Forecasts

### US electronics prices keep climbing
[us-ppi-sectors:computer_electronic: Holt-Winters forecast, 3 ahead](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
The last observation is 120.048 in Aug 2026 (us-ppi-sectors). The tool chose Holt-Winters additive with period 12 and fits the past closely: in-sample MAPE 0.21%, residual sd 0.38 index points. It puts Nov 2026 at 122.60, with a 95% band of 121.29 to 123.91 — the range in which the series has stayed, given how it has moved before, not a promise. Continued monthly gains of about one point are assumed. A tariff change on imported components, or the step-down in the base as 2025's increases drop out of the yoy comparison, would take the outcome outside that band.

### Austrian pharma output flat to firmer
[eu-ipi-sectors:AT|C21: Holt-Winters forecast, 3 ahead](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
The last observation is 160.4 in Jul 2026 (eu-ipi-sectors). Holt-Winters additive, period 12, was chosen; the fit is loose, with in-sample MAPE 5.0% and residual sd 12.1 index points. Oct 2026 is put at 165.7 with a 95% band of 124.7 to 206.8 — wide because this series jumps, and the band only reflects how far past months have strayed from the model. A single plant restart or maintenance shutdown, or Eurostat's revision of the July first estimate, would put the outcome outside it.

### Austrian bills level off near €0.32
[energy-household-eu:AT: Holt-Winters forecast, 2 ahead](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
The last observation is €0.3272/kWh in H2 2025 (energy-household-eu). Holt-Winters additive, period 2, gives €0.3249 for H2 2026 with a 95% band of €0.2904 to €0.3594; in-sample MAPE is 3.3%. The band is what the model's past errors imply, nothing more. This price is part tax and part regulated network charge, so the projection extrapolates administrative decisions as if they were a trend: any new levy relief, or its expiry, moves the series outside the band at once.

## Correlations

- **US semiconductor output vs US electronics PPI** (yoy, 2012-01 to 2026-07, n=175): r = 0.01 at lag 0, strongest |r| = 0.14 at lag −12, not distinguishable from zero (Bartlett band 0.42). Today's price surge does not track chip volumes at any lag in this sample.
- **Austria vs Luxembourg household electricity** (yoy, 2007-S2 to 2025-S2, n=35): r = 0.53, lag 0, clears the usual band at this sample size. The two bills move together in the same halves, consistent with a common wholesale and tax-policy cycle rather than one country leading the other.

## What to watch

- eu-ipi-sectors (last 2026-07): the next release settles whether Austrian pharma's 160.4 was a trough or a new level.
- eu-mining-ipi (last 2026-07): confirms Hungary's 155.7 and whether the April step-up holds.
- us-ppi-sectors (last 2026-08): the September print decides whether electronics inflation stays above 12%.
- eu-hicp and cpi-eu (last 2026-07): shows how much of Europe's electricity jump reached headline inflation.
- cattle-parity and cattle-tr (last 2026-08): due next and unmoved in today's note — the check on whether food chains are quiet.

## Sources

- us-ppi-sectors — BLS producer price indexes by NAICS industry via FRED, not seasonally adjusted, monthly; last 2026-08.
- us-chips — Federal Reserve industrial production via FRED (NAICS 3344, 334), monthly, seasonally adjusted; last 2026-07.
- energy-household-eu — Eurostat nrg_pc_204, band DC, all taxes included, EUR/kWh, semi-annual; last 2025-S2.
- eu-ipi-sectors — Eurostat sts_inpr_m, calendar and seasonally adjusted, 2021=100; last 2026-07.
- eu-mining-ipi — Eurostat sts_inpr_m (B, B06, B07, B08, C24), 2021=100; last 2026-07 in the note, 2026-06 via get_series.
- electricity-mix — Ember Yearly Electricity Data and Energy Institute Statistical Review via Our World in Data, TWh; last 2025 (provisional).
- eu-car-registrations — Eurostat road_eqr_carpda, annual; last 2025.
- macro-external — World Bank World Development Indicators, annual; last 2025.
